english: Whose horses are the swiftest? My horses are big; the guest's foals are bigger. Will you yoke them at this feast? At dawn I will yoke them and drive them to the post (tree). What will you stake if the guest defeats you? Then I will give them to him. He will not defeat me. May Dyews give you victory. Dear one, you are very swift(?).

Grandfather told me a tale of your youth. In my youth I was the swiftest of all men. I won nine prizes. Which prize is the greatest? A king gave me a white horse. Where is it now? It died, and its foals stand in our field. Are they strong? They are strong, and I will yoke them in summer.
uncertain: question has fem.pl ish₁réh₂s but the foals are masc.; answer ish₁rós looks like nom.sg — possible agreement problem

english: Where did your brother's spear fall? It fell into the thicket. The herdsman pointed his spear toward the river. The wind took my spear. The wind is not (calm?) at this feast. Sister, be silent. I remember the great boasts you spoke yesterday. Tomorrow I will show, and you will see.
uncertain: 'the wind at this feast is not' — predicate missing?

english: Why, child, are you lying here? The king's two grandsons ... the village and threw(?) me down. Is your leg broken? Not broken; my arm burns. I will heal your arm with warm water. Grandmother, you are very kind. Will you take them on tomorrow? I will seize them and throw them.
uncertain: ní ... déyḱt 'showed down' odd — maybe should be a 'throw' verb

english: Old man, will you sing against the guest? I sing, and my song will be sweeter than his songs. What do you sing? The fame of the men who killed the snake. He sings songs of wolves to the guests. The households love his songs. The elders give me a cup. The gods hear your voice.
uncertain: kéh₂nmn̥-kʷe moy ... swéh₂dyos: neuter noun with masc comparative?
gʰostíbʰos wĺ̥kʷōm kéh₂nmn̥h₂ séngʷʰeti — who sings is unclear

english: Herdsman, will you throw the stone very far? What will you give me if I win? A ram of the sheep. If you beat me, what shall I give you? A young dog. A dog for me? It is much dearer than a hundred sheep. Now, herdsman, you have feared me. I feared nobody. Now go on (be).
uncertain: h₁éy 'they' plural for a single dog?
